topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: A 0.25 dB passband loss directly affects signal power within the desired frequency band, leading to a decrease in maximum allowed path loss or an increase in required transmitter power. The increased noise floor due to passband loss reduces the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), impacting capacity and reliability. This reduction in SNR necessitates more sensitive amplifiers or larger antennas to compensate for the loss, resulting in decreased link availability. The impact on system/network implications is a decrease in data throughput and an increase in latency due to retransmissions.
